sources.title: World Imagery: bounded western Ozama-area chosen-opening and first eastward valley detail
sources.publication_identity: Same independent photographic publication; a sequential, distinct detail of this researched Dominican opening, unrelated to any held selected view.
sources.actual_material_read: Complete original detail, its unmarked western crop and corresponding private orientation aid, read across the chosen opening and early receiving corridor.
sources.supports: Northgoing opening valley, first northeast/east bend, tributary-side terrain and eastward receiving valley.
sources.limits: Small cloud/shadow areas remain over portions of the western bend. Ordinary topographic/floodplain continuation is supported; exact wet thread, current flow, spring identity and headwater name are not established.

correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening descends south from an upland hollow into a narrow, vegetated dry-channel valley before turning southeast. The complete imagery and clean opening enlargement show this descent and its joining side gullies. The municipal relief map clips away part of the opening at its western boundary; that missing map footprint is supplied by independent imagery, not by an extrapolated municipal stream label. No named spring or official headwater is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection follows the southeastward valley through successive tributary joins between dissected uplands. Chihuahua’s original relief plate directly labels this receiving corridor El Álamo. Imagery shows the same continuous valley, its pale channel floor and the opening toward the eastern plain. The label is bounded to the named upper receiving reach; it is not extended back to the exact chosen opening by proximity alone.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The long stored part leaves the confined El Álamo valley, crosses its broad eastern fan/receiving floor among fields and turns north along the eastern side of the interior plain. The map shows the connected upper drainage and northward receiving network; the imagery supplies the full broad fan and turn where the generalized line and local channel traces do not coincide exactly. The ordinary continuous alluvial floor establishes this connection without requiring one currently wet channel or asserting irrigation operation.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selected eastern northward passage follows the lowland corridor in the Laguna El Diablo setting, west of the eastern relief and south of the mapped El Sauz label. The relief plate distinguishes this intermittent lake/playa name from Laguna Palomas farther east and Encinillas farther north. The imagery shows a continuous pale, locally cultivated and channel-marked receiving floor. The passage is treated at lake/playa-corridor scale, not as a uniformly exposed river reach or a verified present lake shoreline.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The route bends northwest into the broader northward axial receiving corridor directly labeled El Sauz on the original relief map, then continues toward Encinillas. Western and eastern side washes join that same corridor. The map separately labels the western La Campana branch; that tributary name is not a river alias or a name assigned to the selected western opening. Imagery shows the uninterrupted valley/playa floor and joining fan traces along all these parts. Broad-floor continuity, rather than exact modern wet-thread tracing, establishes the through-link.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: encinillas lake approach and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The last northward reach swings northwest along the lake-receiving floor and enters the waterbody mapped as Encinillas. The actual coincident source and render endings fall within the selected lake-interior setting, not at an invented farther shore or downstream extension. Both the original municipal plate and complete imagery show the final approach and lake. No claim is made about present water level, permanent surface discharge or an official terminal coordinate.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening follows a forest-covered headward hollow westward and then southwest between dissected ridges toward the exposed foothill river. The detailed original distinguishes this valley setting from the adjoining ridges and parallel drainages. Canopy and small clouds obscure the exact small channel, but do not create a separate-basin or missing valley-transfer problem. No tiny source-channel name or source monument is assigned.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: foothill exit and westward alluvial passage
correspondence.finding: The western continuation leaves the hill front and crosses the broad cultivated alluvial floor. Visible river meanders, branching channel traces and adjoining riparian strips occupy the same receiving corridor. The selected southern jog simplifies this floodplain passage; it is not treated as a surveyed current thread or a different basin.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection turns north and northwest beside the connected meandering river through agricultural lowland. Tributary approaches descend from the eastern foothills into this same river corridor. The basin study associates the upper León with Villarteaga and records the Villarteaga bridge on the Chigorodó–Mutatá road; that broad upper association does not establish a precise name-transition vertex.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestward middle river and barranquillita setting
correspondence.finding: The river continues northwest through fields and a broader riparian/floodplain belt, passing road and settlement settings before bending more northerly. The study independently identifies the León crossing at Barranquillita. The image supplies continuity through the actual selection rather than inferring a path from the place name alone.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: middle northward river and wetland approach
correspondence.finding: The lower-gradient corridor bends north past distinct tributary joins into an increasingly broad wetland and floodplain belt. The selected western bends and their receiving continuation remain within this connected river corridor. Haze and small cloud patches limit banks and minor-thread detail, not the ordinary geographic through-link.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The nearly northward modeled interval generalizes a sinuous river with riparian wetlands, side channels, fields and eastern tributary entries. The complete original shows the common connected alluvial corridor throughout. No lake-to-feeder transfer or separate basin is required, and no claim is made that the straight selected cells reproduce the present meanders.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower wetland bend and stage join
correspondence.finding: The corridor turns northeast and then east across the lower wetland plain, following the connected river passage toward the broader northward coastal channel. The junction and end of FID11304 remain in this common river setting. The stage boundary is a stored subdivision, not demonstrated hydronym change.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: From the stage join, the broad lower channel runs north and northeast beside developed agricultural/transport ground on its eastern side and wetlands to the west. Its successive bends lead into the terminal coastal reach visible in the same original.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: separate source and render terminal settings
correspondence.finding: The stored source endpoint lies in the lower river-mouth approach. The separately stored render endpoint extends northwest toward the inner-gulf coastal opening. Both belong to the visible connected mouth and coastal receiving setting, consistent with the study’s Golfo de Urabá destination. They are preserved separately; neither is promoted to an exact surveyed shoreline intersection or a present-flow measurement.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen upper hollow and westward descent
correspondence.finding: The chosen northeastern opening occupies a shallow west-trending drainage hollow between dissected hills. The visible receiving hollow continues west and southwest into the broader valley at the western bend. The pale small pans farther northeast are outside this selected route; no connection through them is asserted. Fine channel threads are locally faint, but the same connected receiving hollow is visible at ordinary terrain scale.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: western bend and southward receiving valley
correspondence.finding: The upper hollow opens into a broad southward alluvial valley along the western side of the central hill mass. Several western gullies and a larger western approach join this same floor near the southern turn. The selected bend and join do not require an inter-basin crossing; no name is assigned from the unlabeled photograph.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The collector turns southeast through a pale, locally broad alluvial corridor at the foot of the central hills, then narrows and bends south. Lateral fan and gully arrivals enter the same valley. All six stored parts correspond to this ordinary continuous receiving corridor; diffuse dry areas are not treated as missing hydraulic links.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: central collector and eastern tributary arrival
correspondence.finding: A south-trending corridor contains a winding darker or vegetated strip with broad pale marginal patches. A separately visible northeastward valley approaches the collector from the east; its joining fan and the western selected continuation share the same open valley floor. The southward sequence continues through the central broadening. Small clouds and shadows occur mainly on neighboring slopes and do not interrupt the ordinary receiving-floor correspondence. No exact present wet thread, salinity, land use or tributary name is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southwestern turn and lower valley entry
correspondence.finding: The collector bends southwest along a continuous light alluvial strip, then returns south into a more confined lower valley. Side gullies converge from adjacent hills. Local coarse-selection displacement is preserved rather than corrected; the valley connection remains visible without any transfer to a separate basin.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower dry valley and widening floor
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows a long south to southeast dry valley between low hills and enters a broad receiving floor. Multiple channel traces and lateral alluvial approaches occupy the same contiguous floor. There is no substantial missing basin-to-feeder transfer in these parts, and no requirement for a continuously wet modern channel is imposed.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The lower corridor turns southeast across a broad, flat fan-like receiving area toward the western margin of the pale closed depression. The intervening floor is continuously visible and has diffuse drainage traces; it is not divided from the terminal depression by an observed separate basin or hill barrier. A road crosses the area, but current drainage operation or engineered controls are not established.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The last selected part continues from the western marginal drainage area into the pale interior lake/playa floor beside a darker marginal strip. The source-end and render-end metadata are separately retained and coincide in the supplied selection. Both correspond to this interior receiving-floor location. The selected ending is not extended to the far shore, assigned to a surveyed bank, or described as an ocean or through-river mouth. Contemporary water coverage and the lake label at this precise place remain unverified.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The chosen opening occupies a narrow northgoing valley between dissected, partly cultivated hills. The detail shows the receiving valley, its tributary side valleys and continuation toward the wider bend. Small cloud/shadow patches conceal sections of the channel, but the ordinary valley floor and bounding terrain establish the receiving corridor without requiring a continuously visible wet thread. The chosen vertex is not asserted to be the natural spring, nor assigned a separate headwater hydronym.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The valley bends northeast and east into a broader alluvial strip, with open fields, wooded stream margins and lateral tributary valleys. Local clouds obscure thread detail near the western bend; visible terrain on both sides and the adjoining continuous valley support ordinary geographic continuation. Farther east, visible sinuous water and riparian linework follow the selected receiving valley below forested slopes.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection follows the same eastward foothill corridor through successive small bends and widening alluvial pockets. The original detail and overlapping overview expose the receiving valley and separate side valleys; the generalized selected line does not precisely trace every meander.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The river corridor turns northeast through foothill meanders and reaches its northern bend. The visible river, wooded floodplain and valley margins connect the successive selected parts. Small scattered clouds affect local detail rather than establishing a separate basin or broken corridor.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: Beyond the northern turn, the selection runs south through a continuous cultivated and settled valley with a sinuous river and lateral tributary approaches. The main receiving corridor remains distinguishable from those lateral branches through all four stored parts.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The river bends east across a broader alluvial plain. Tributary-side corridors meet the main floodplain, which remains continuous through the selected turn. Patchy clouds near the western approach limit exact channel observation but do not hide the practical valley-to-plain receiving connection.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: A broad vegetated river/floodplain corridor continues southeast, with cultivated margins and meandering water among riparian vegetation. The selection stays within the ordinary receiving corridor through the short stored-part joins.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The lower river bends east, receives a distinct eastern-side approach, then continues south through its wet lowland corridor. The photographed meeting place, adjoining floodplain and downstream meanders support geographic continuity. Individual tributary names are not assigned to a join solely from the image.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The river turns southwest through a wide wetland/floodplain and enters the urban fringe. The visible lower river, elongated vegetated margins and narrowing urban approach continue across the stored parts; adjacent wetland channels are not substituted for the selected main receiver.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.

correspondence.finding: The urban river continues southwest, meets a broad western tributary approach, then turns south through the port channel to the coastal opening. The rendered ending is at the inner harbor-mouth setting; the separate source ending lies slightly farther seaward at the coastal receiving opening. Both are preserved as distinct endpoint descriptions. The municipal plan independently names the Ozama receiving system and its Caribbean outlet, with San Soucí at the mouth. No exact shoreline, tidal boundary, present navigational depth or active-flow assertion is made.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the listed fragment.
